blocks.h2: Basement Flooding in Tinley Park Homes
blocks.intro: Tinley Park has been part of seven federal flood disaster declarations since 1972, including 2013 and 2023. In April 2013, heavy overnight rain closed several Tinley Park streets, and the village fielded calls about flooded basements.

items.body: Storms that flood basements often knock out power too. A [sump pump](/tinley-park/sump-pumps) without a battery backup stops right when you need it.

blocks.h2: Basement Waterproofing
bodies: Waterproofing is the fix when groundwater pushes through the foundation, not when it comes up a drain. Signs include damp walls, water along the joint between the wall and floor, white powdery deposits on the concrete and puddles after rain with no drain backing up.

Interior drain tile and a [sump pump](/tinley-park/sump-pumps) work together: the tile collects the water and the pump sends it out and away. Before recommending anything, we confirm the water is coming through the foundation, not from a leak or a sewer backup, so you don't pay for the wrong fix.

items.q: Should I call a plumber or a restoration company first?
items.preview: A plumber, if water is still coming in. Cleanup only works once the source is stopped.

items.q: Why does my Tinley Park basement only flood in big storms?
items.preview: Big storms overwhelm sump pumps and fill sewers. The cause decides the fix.
items.answer: In a normal rain, your sump pump and sewer line keep up. In a big storm, groundwater rises faster than an older pump can move it, the power may go out or the sewer fills and pushes water back through the floor drain. We'll find out which happened in your basement.

blocks.h2: What Does a Catch Basin Do?
blocks.body: A catch basin is a buried box at a low point in the yard or at the bottom of a driveway. Rain and runoff flow in through the grate, dirt and leaves settle to the bottom, and the water leaves through a pipe. When the sump at the bottom fills, debris blocks the outlet and the water stays in your yard. We clean basins, clear outlet pipes and repair basins that have cracked or sunk.

A full basin sends water toward the house instead of away from it.

items.q: How often should I clean my catch basin?
items.preview: Once a year for basins under trees, ideally in fall. Others less often.
items.answer: Basins under mature trees usually need cleaning once a year, best after the leaves drop. Basins in open lawns can go longer. If water sits around the grate after rain, it's due.

items.q: Is a catch basin the same as a French drain?
items.preview: No. A catch basin collects surface water at one low spot. A French drain collects groundwater along a trench.
items.answer: No. A catch basin collects surface water at a low point and sends it out through a pipe. A French drain is a gravel-filled trench with a perforated pipe that collects water along its length. We clean and repair catch basins and the pipes that serve them.

items.q: Can a clogged catch basin flood my basement?
items.preview: Yes. Water that can't drain pools against the foundation.
items.answer: It can. When the basin can't drain, water collects along the foundation and works its way into the sump pit or the basement.

blocks.h2: Kitchen Sink Drain Unclogging
bodies: Kitchen sinks clog slowly, then all at once. Grease, starch and coffee grounds coat the pipe until water stops moving. Garbage disposals add to it when food goes down without enough water behind it.

If water backs up into the other side of the sink, or the dishwasher drains into it, the clog is past the trap. We clear the line with a cable, check it toward the main and show you what came out. blocks.body: Basement bathrooms and laundry rooms usually sit lower than the sewer line leaving the house, so they can't drain by gravity. Their drains run into a sealed basin in the floor. blocks.h2: What Is Hydro Jetting?
blocks.body: Hydro jetting clears a sewer line with a high-pressure water stream, fed through the same cleanout access point used for rodding. A specialized nozzle sprays water in every direction as it moves through the pipe, scouring grease, scale, and roots off the entire pipe wall instead of just cutting a path through the middle. It's the fix for buildup that keeps coming back after rodding, or for roots that have worked into the pipe joints. Rodding opens the line back up. Hydro jetting cleans it.

img.alt: Diagram showing how hydro jetting clears a residential sewer line, with a cross-section view of the underground pipe, jet nozzle, high-pressure water spray, and debris being flushed toward the street connection

blocks.h2: When Your Plumbing Needs Hydro Jetting
blocks.intro: Jetting earns its keep when a line needs a deep clean:

tiles.body: A sagging section collects sludge that a rod pushes around but doesn't remove. Jetting flushes it out.
A rod leaves root stubs behind. Jetting cuts them flush with the pipe wall, so regrowth is slower.

tiles.h3: A Kitchen Line Coated in Grease
tiles.body: Years of grease narrow the line one layer at a time until the sink backs up.

tiles.h3: Before Lining or After a Big Backup
tiles.body: A pipe has to be clean for a liner to bond, and a line that just backed up is full of debris.

blocks.h2: Why Hydro Jetting Works for Tinley Park Lines
blocks.intro: Most Tinley Park homes have sewer lines from the 1970s through the 2000s. Jetting is often the best way to clean them without digging anything up.

items.body: Newer lines have fewer rough spots than old clay, so once they're jetted clean, they tend to stay clean longer.

We check every line on camera before jetting. If a section is cracked or separated, we'll tell you and suggest [rodding](/tinley-park/sewer-rodding) or a repair instead.

blocks.h2: Does Your Tinley Park Basement Need an Overhead Sewer?
blocks.intro: Here's how to tell the connection, not a clog, is the problem:

tiles.h3: Water Rises at the Floor Drain in Every Big Storm

No roots, no sag, no crack on camera, and it still backs up in heavy rain.

tiles.h3: A Finished Basement Has Already Taken a Hit
tiles.body: One cleanup of carpet and drywall is enough to look for a permanent fix.

blocks.h2: How an Overhead Sewer System Works
blocks.body: Your upstairs drains already flow out above the level where the sewer can back up. An overhead system does the same for the basement. The floor drain, basement toilet, shower and laundry are rerouted into a sealed pit. An [ejector pump](/tinley-park/ejector-pump) lifts that wastewater up to a new line near the ceiling, and a check valve stops it from flowing back. From there, gravity carries it out to the sewer.

blocks.h2: Overhead Sewers and Tinley Park Basements
blocks.intro: Tinley Park has been included in federal flood disaster declarations in 1986, 1987, 1993, 2013 and 2023. Homes that back up in those storms tend to do it again.

items.body: If your basement is finished, with a bedroom, family room or bathroom, that's a lot to lose to one storm.

items.h3: Basement Bathrooms Need a Pump Anyway
items.body: If your basement already has an ejector pump for a bathroom, a conversion builds on what's there.
We camera the sewer line before recommending a conversion. If a sag or a root mat is the real cause, a [repair](/tinley-park/sewer-repair) may be all you need.

blocks.h2: What Is Sewer Rodding?
blocks.body: Sewer rodding clears a blocked main line with a long, flexible steel cable fed through a cleanout access point. A cutting head on the end breaks through roots, grease, and debris and pushes the blockage toward the street connection, restoring flow through the pipe. It's the standard first fix for a clogged or backed-up sewer line. For most homes, it's the only fix needed.

blocks.h2: What Is Trenchless Sewer Repair?
blocks.body: Trenchless sewer repair, also called no-dig sewer repair, fixes a damaged pipe without digging a trench along its full length. Instead of opening up your yard from the house to the street, we work through one or two access points and repair the pipe from the inside or replace it in place. There are two main methods: cured-in-place pipe (CIPP) lining and pipe bursting. Both fix the line underground, so what's above it stays untouched.

img.alt: Two J. Blanton plumbers setting up sewer camera and cable equipment beside a home's foundation before a trenchless sewer repair

blocks.h2: Why Trenchless Fits Tinley Park Homes
blocks.intro: About 87% of Tinley Park homes are owner-occupied, and many owners have spent years on patios, landscaping and finished yards. A repair that skips the trench protects that work.

items.body: In many subdivisions, the sewer line runs under the driveway or a backyard patio. Lining or bursting the pipe in place leaves them alone.
Roots from mature trees get into loose joints and fittings. A liner seals every joint at once, so they can't get back in.
A liner follows the shape of the old pipe. If the line has a deep sag, we may recommend a spot repair for that section and lining for the rest.

blocks.h2: When Does Trenchless Apply?
blocks.intro: Backups, slow drains, sewer odor, soft or unusually lush patches of grass, and gurgling drains are the most common signs of a damaged sewer line. Which repair method fits comes down to the type and extent of the damage.
head: Situation
Trenchless Usually Works

rows: Corroded or aging clay, cast iron, or Orangeburg pipe

blocks.note: Not sure which category applies to your line? A [camera inspection](/tinley-park/video-camera-sewer-inspections) shows exactly what's happening underground before any repair method gets recommended.

blocks.h2: How Trenchless Sewer Repair Works in Tinley Park
blocks.intro: The camera decides which method fits your line.

steps.body: We clean the pipe, pull in a resin-soaked liner and cure it in place. It hardens into a seamless new pipe inside the old one. Our trucks use light-cured lining, which sets faster than older steam or water methods.
If the old pipe is too damaged to line, a bursting head breaks it apart while pulling a new pipe in behind it. No trench along the line.
We record the line before we recommend a method and again when we finish. You get a flat rate before work starts.

blocks.h2: Signs Your Water Heater Needs Repair
blocks.intro: Here's what Tinley Park homeowners usually notice first:

tiles.body: A heater that can't keep up may have sediment taking up space, a failing element or a burner that isn't firing fully.

tiles.h3: A Wet Spot Under the Tank
tiles.body: A drip from a valve or fitting can usually be fixed. Water from the tank body means the tank is done.
Sediment on the bottom of the tank pops as the burner heats through it.
A worn thermocouple or flame sensor shuts the gas off. It's one of the most common repairs we make.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Problems in Tinley Park Homes

items.h3: Whole Neighborhoods on the Same Schedule
items.body: Subdivisions built in the same few years tend to replace water heaters around the same time too. If your neighbors are replacing theirs, check the date on yours.

items.h3: Families Use a Lot of Hot Water
items.body: Homes built for families run laundry, dishwashers and back-to-back showers. A heater sized for the original household may be working past its limit.
Midway Airport averages about 5 nights a year at or below zero. Incoming water is coldest then, so the heater runs longest, and a weak one gives out.

blocks.h2: Residential Water Heater Service
bodies: We work on the water heaters found in Tinley Park homes: standard gas tanks, power-vent models, electric units and tankless heaters in basements, laundry rooms and garages. Every visit starts with a diagnosis before any recommendation.

Not sure what you have? Look at the label on the side of the tank. It shows the fuel, the size and when it was made. Read it to us when you call. If you're ready for a new one, see [water heater installation](/tinley-park/water-heater-installation).

blocks.h2: Water Heater Maintenance and Flushing
bodies: A yearly flush drains the sediment that collects at the bottom of every tank. Left alone, it makes the heater slower, louder and shorter-lived. During a maintenance visit, we also check the anode rod, the relief valve and the burner or elements.

Most manufacturers suggest flushing about once a year, and tankless units need regular descaling. If your heater has never been flushed and it's more than a few years old, start there before assuming it needs replacing.

blocks.h2: Water Heater Questions From Tinley Park Homeowners

items.q: How long should a water heater last in Tinley Park?
items.preview: Tank heaters typically last about 8 to 12 years. Tankless units often last longer.
items.answer: Tank heaters typically last about 8 to 12 years, and tankless units often last longer with regular descaling. If yours is close to that age and acting up, a repair may not be worth it.

items.q: Should I repair or replace my water heater?
items.preview: A leaking tank means replace. A failed part on a younger heater is usually a repair.
items.answer: If the tank is leaking, it needs replacing. If a part failed and the heater is under about 8 years old, a repair usually makes sense. If the repair would cost a big share of a new heater, we'll tell you.

items.q: Why is my water heater leaking from the bottom?
items.preview: Either a valve, which is a repair, or the tank, which means replacement.
items.answer: A dripping drain valve or relief valve is a repair. A tank that's corroded through means replacement. Shut off the water to the heater and call. We'll tell you which one it is.

items.q: How much does water heater repair cost in Tinley Park?
items.preview: It depends on the part and the heater. You get a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on what failed, the heater type and the parts it needs. We diagnose first and give you a flat-rate price before any work begins.

items.q: How often should a water heater be serviced?
items.preview: About once a year for a tank flush. Tankless units need regular descaling.
items.answer: Most manufacturers recommend flushing a tank heater about once a year and descaling tankless units regularly. An annual check also catches a worn anode rod or a sticky relief valve early. See [water heater maintenance](#water-heater-maintenance).
